name: Satisfactory Dedicated Server
description: Install the official Satisfactory dedicated server through SteamCMD and launch its native Windows server executable without a shell.
known_limitations: A new server must be claimed and given its administrator password through Satisfactory's in-game Server Manager; these values are not exposed as ineffective GameNode variables.

GameNode does not call Satisfactory's HTTPS management API. Stop now sends a targeted Windows console interrupt (the compiled console_interrupt runtime stop type) instead of terminating the process outright, but real-world graceful-shutdown acceptance against a running Satisfactory dedicated server is still pending; see the compatibility findings below.
A server rediscovered after a GameNode restart cannot receive a safely addressed console interrupt and falls back to GameNode's terminate lifecycle for that stop.
Satisfactory may automatically increment the primary port if it becomes unavailable after GameNode's preflight; GameNode does not automatically discover or re-register that changed port.
Automatic updates, mods, save management, and HTTPS API management are outside this template.

variables.name: Server port
variables.description: Primary Satisfactory port used for TCP server/API traffic and UDP game/query traffic.

variables.name: Reliable messaging port
variables.description: TCP port used by Satisfactory reliable messaging. It must be forwarded in addition to the primary port.

variables.name: Maximum players
variables.description: Player cap passed through Satisfactory's documented GameSession startup setting. Values above four can increase resource usage and instability.

variables.name: Release branch
variables.description: Install the normal public build or the official experimental Steam branch.

ports.name: Game/query
ports.purpose: Game traffic and lightweight query API

config_files.description: Optional advanced Windows server configuration generated by Satisfactory after runtime use.

requirements.description: Managed anonymous SteamCMD installation is required.
Satisfactory Dedicated Server requires an x86-64 host.
Ensure sufficient storage for the current dedicated-server build and future save data.
Larger saves and player counts can require substantially more memory and CPU time.

help.summary: GameNode installs Satisfactory with anonymous SteamCMD and launches FactoryServer.exe directly without a command shell.
notes: After first start, claim the server and configure administrator/player passwords through Satisfactory's in-game Server Manager.
The primary port is registered for both TCP and UDP; the reliable messaging port is registered for TCP.
Satisfactory 1.0 no longer uses the historical ports 15000 and 15777.

Stop uses GameNode's compiled console_interrupt runtime stop type: a targeted Windows console interrupt (CTRL_BREAK) scoped to this process's own process group, not a broadcast, not stdin text, and not an HTTPS shutdown hook. If the process does not exit before the configured timeout, GameNode falls back to its existing bounded force-kill path.
A server rediscovered after a GameNode restart stops through GameNode's terminate lifecycle instead, because its original console cannot be safely reattached.

findings.summary: The Windows console_interrupt runtime stop path is implemented and covered by automated tests, but has not yet been verified against a real running Satisfactory dedicated server; compatibility stays partially_compatible until that real-world acceptance passes.
Server claim, name, administrator password, and player password are managed through Satisfactory's Server Manager rather than template variables.

prerequisites: Network access to Steam content servers
Sufficient storage for server files and saves
